newsitem.title: UK: Consumer goods, finance power ahead over 1 yr - MSCI.
newsitem.headline: Consumer goods, finance power ahead over 1 yr - MSCI.

text.p: Among global equity investors, the consumer goods and finance sectors have proved top performers over the 12 months to end September, the latest data from Morgan Stanley Capital International (MSCI) shows.
In a monthly report, MSCI said it ranked eight industry sectors in 22 developed markets over the period.
Consumer Goods returned 20.4 percent in dollar terms, with no dividends, Finance 10.7 percent, Capital Equipment 10.6 percent, Energy 10.1 percent and Services 9.9 percent.
They were tailed by Materials, returning 6.8 percent, "multi-industry" 6.5 percent and Gold Mines, with negative 4.5 percent returns.
MSCI also analysed data from the top two sectors to determine current value.

The MSCI Consumer Goods Index gained over 20 percent in recent months to reach its all-time high of 892.9 at September 30. The sector was the best on an annualised basis for the past two, five and 10 uyears at 19.8 percent, 10.9 percent and 12.2 percent respectively.
It also outperformed the MSCI World index (where it accounts for 21.9 percent by market capitalisation) in each period.

But MSCI said that the price to book value ratio (P/BV) has also reached a new high at 3.6, significantly higher than any other sector. "This is a cautionary tale to value-driven investors," the MSCI report warned.
The Finance sector was the second best performer, also reaching an all-time high of 660.9 at the end of Q3. It returned 10.7 percent in dollar terms, no dividends reinvested.
Over the past two, five and 10 years the sector has returned 10.7 percent, 8.3 percent and 7.3 percent, but has underperformed the World Index in each period.

Amongst top performing stocks in developed markets in the last three months, MSCI identified Malaysia's Rachid Hussain, up 83.7 percent, American PWR Conversion up 81.9 percent, Australia'a TNT up 76.1 percent, Threecom Corp up 71.7 percent and MFS Communications Co up 59.1 percent.

MSCI said the five worst performing stocks amongst developed markets were Foxmeyer Health Corp, down 67.3 percent, Singapore's Amcol Holdings, down 67.2 percent, Spain's Huarte, down 67 percent, DSC Communications Corp, down 53.8 percent and Laboratory Corp of America, down 50.9 percent.
